The symmetry is hard to resist. Both directives are strings at the top of a file, both say where code runs, and the React docs place them side by side. React's own Server Components page calls this "a common misunderstanding", which tells you how many people have made it. The half that's true:
does draw a line between server and client code. It's just a different line, drawn around functions the client may call, not around components the server renders.

React's reference states it directly: "there is no directive for Server Components." In an app built on them, everything is a Server Component unless it's defined in, or imported through, a module marked

. So making a page a Server Component takes no code at all. You only ever mark the other side: the point where client code starts. The page in the opening was a Server Component before anyone touched it; the directive changed only what the browser is allowed to call.
'use server' marks functions the client can call
goes at the top of an async function's body, or at the top of a file. Either way it creates

. The framework passes the client a reference instead of the code, and when client code calls that reference, React sends a network request with a serialized copy of the arguments, runs the function on the server and sends back the serialized result. That's why the directive works only on async functions, and why arguments are limited to serializable values like strings, plain objects and

blocks.title: Every Server Function is a public endpoint

content.text: React's docs call Server Functions "exposed server endpoints" and their arguments "fully client-controlled". Your UI may only ever pass the ids it rendered, but anyone can send the request with different ones. Validate every argument, and check inside each function that the logged-in user may perform that action.

blocks.title: Don't fetch data through Server Functions

content.text: reference says Server Functions are designed for mutations, not data fetching: frameworks that implement them "typically process one action at a time and do not have a way to cache the return value". Read data in the Server Component itself, as
, and keep Server Functions for changes.
